F3 tie-break: the halved carry leaves two boats level, RRS A8 cannot separate them, and the final-series ranking decides the championship

ILCA 7 2026 — World Championship, Dun Laoghaire IRL · F3 · D3, D7 · SI (reference-docs:events/ilca7-worlds-2026/SI-with-Amendment-2.md)

2 qualifying fleets · → Gold/Silver · discards: 1 discard from race 3. · medal race ×1
This is the Amendment 2 text. Amendment 3 (22 August 2026) replaced SI
18.7.4 with a plain last-race comparison in place of RRS A8, which is
fixture 18 — so what follows is no longer how this particular championship
breaks its ties. It stays because the clause itself is not unusual: an
SI that keeps A8 and adds sub-series steps behind it is a shape a scorer
still meets, and `medal.tieBreak: stage-rank` still means it.

Two SI clauses meet here, and the first is why the second exists:

  18.7.3  … the Qualification series scores are divided by 2 (two), rounded
          to the nearest whole number (0.5 rounded upward).
  18.7.4  For boats qualified to compete in the Final series, ties will be
          broken applying RRS A8. If a tie remains between two or more
          boats, it will be broken in favour of the boat which was ranked
          higher in the Elimination series, then Preliminary series.

Rounding a score to a whole number manufactures ties: any two boats one
point apart arrive at the Final series level. That is exactly what happens
to y1 and y2 below — 7 points each, so 4 each once halved (3.5 rounds up).

The Final series is then not sailed at all, which under SI 18.7.5 makes the
adjusted scores the event result. So y1 and y2 finish on 4 with a single
identical score between them: A8.1 compares two identical lists and A8.2
has no race to walk back through. Without SI 18.7.4 the championship's
second and third places would be undecided.

The clause settles it on the Elimination series alone — the final-stage
races scored as their own series. y1 sailed them 2nd and 2nd (4 points),
y2 3rd and 3rd (6), so y1 takes second overall. Note this reverses their
qualifying form: y2 out-scored y1 across the Preliminary series (2 to 3),
which is why the clause reaches for the Elimination series *first* and only
falls back to the Preliminary series behind it.

Hand check, DNC base 4 throughout, one discard from 3 races, at most one of
them from the final series:
  b1  Q 1,1,1  F 1,1  -> discard a 1        = 4  -> halved 2
  y1  Q 1,2,2  F 2,2  -> discard Q2's 2     = 7  -> halved 4
  y2  Q 2,1,1  F 3,3  -> discard F1's 3     = 7  -> halved 4
